brief: My Own Sunrise — English female motivational soul-pop. 120 seconds, approximately 96 BPM, syncopated 4/4. Rhodes, rounded bass, tight drums, handclaps and backing harmonies. Start vulnerable and grow into confident, joyful singing. Include a sparse bridge. Hook: “I can be my own sunrise / Watch me open up the skies”. Test expressive phrasing and harmonies without burying the lead.

lyrics.text:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
Four a.m., I'm tracing cracks along the ceiling
Cold tea on the sill, my phone face down and dim
I rehearse the speech I never get to say out loud
Pull your old sweater on, still doubting where I begin

[Chorus]
I can be my own sunrise
Watch me open up the skies
Gold on my shoulders, bare feet on the floor
I'm done waiting on a light to knock on my door

[Verse 2]
Now the kettle's singing and I'm humming right along
Curtains pulled wide, honey sliding off my spoon
I catch my grin in the window, steady and strong
Dancing through the kitchen, a slow and easy tune

[Bridge]
Hush now, it was me holding the match
Just me, and the quiet, and my breath
Soft, soft, I felt it start to catch
Warm on my skin, no fear left

[Chorus]
I can be my own sunrise
Watch me open up the skies
Gold on my shoulders, bare feet on the floor
I'm done waiting on a light to knock on my door

[Outro]
lyrics.topic: A woman moves from doubt to self-belief: the verses start vulnerable and concrete, the chorus is confident and joyful, the bridge is sparse and quiet before the last chorus.

flavour: syncopated soul-pop, starts vulnerable then grows joyful, harmonies never bury the lead
